results.title: Georgia bet big on EV manufacturing. Trump pulled the plug. - Grist
results.content:
Georgia-based bus manufacturer Blue Bird started selling electric buses commercially in 2018 and built an expanded factory for electric buses in 2023. In 2022, Hyundai built a plant near Savannah that it said would be dedicated to making EVs. In 2024, Kia started making EVs at its West Point plant. And in 2025, Rivian broke ground on its manufacturing plant near Atlanta. The Hyundai and Rivian operations are two of the biggest economic development projects in Georgia history. The state has also [...] The state has also worked to attract other parts of the EV and clean energy manufacturing sector, including battery makers and recyclers and solar panel companies. [...] Georgia leads the region in EV and battery manufacturing, but the growth has stumbled, with layoffs at SK Battery earlier this year. More than $4 billion in investment has been canceled or scaled back in the last year across the Southeast, according to SACE.

That’s dwarfed, though, by the nearly $74 billion in manufacturing investment that’s moving ahead. Still, one open question, Cross said, is whether Georgians will buy the hybrids and EVs being made in the state.

results.title: Georgia is plugged in to electric transportation
results.content:
Original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) in Georgia and throughout the Southeast region are already shifting their product lines to keep up with the increasing production of EV vehicles. This trend will only expand as more suppliers flock to the region’s robust electric vehicle ecosystem. [...] Several additional EV companies from Korea, Germany, Turkey and beyond have all opened EV manufacturing operations in Georgia, and more companies are on their way.

What’s Next for the State’s EV Industry? [...] A steady stream of EV companies has already set up shop in Georgia over the past several years. Most recently, Rivian, Inc. selected Georgia for a nearly 13 million square foot plant for vehicle and battery operations. Rivian will invest $5 billion in a carbon-conscious campus in Georgia for its electric adventure vehicles. Across operations, Rivian will create approximately 7,500 jobs. In 2019, South Korea-based SK Innovations broke ground on two massive EV battery plants in Jackson County.

Additionally, the recycling and disposal of batteries pose unique logistical challenges.
